prize_parts.citation: for expanding the genetic code with orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs that install designed non-canonical amino acids at chosen sites in proteins in living cells
for the development of base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of DNA bases without double-strand cleavage

statement.case_for: After the first round my configuration is unchanged: genetic code expansion (Schultz and Chin) plus base editing (Liu), three people in all. Both are inventions in which chemists rebuilt a piece of cellular machinery into a general tool. Orthogonal synthetase/tRNA pairs place a designed side chain at a chosen site in a living cell, and that has been reproduced for over twenty years and underlies bioorthogonal handles, crosslinkers and designed protein materials. Base editing uses evolved deaminase fusions to make a defined chemical change in DNA, with about ten years of independent validation and early clinical use. Schultz and Chin are the founding and the generalising leaders of the code-expansion work, and Liu is the clear leader of base editing, so the three-name limit does not force a cut that I find hard to defend scientifically. What round 1 did change is my ranking of the fallbacks: I now think B037 is the stronger fallback and would accept it as the committee's prize if it moves to a majority.
statement.case_against: The weakest point is still B002 credit. Omitting Lei Wang, Ryan Mehl and Shigeyuki Yokoyama is a judgement, and Peter Somfai is right that this attribution is as entangled as B037. The second weakness is B060: Andrei Chabes and Peter Somfai, who both ranked it first or third at the opening, have moved it to an alternative because of the 2020 CRISPR prize and the unresolved Nishida and Kondo priority question, and clinical safety data are still accumulating. A third weakness is that no other member prefers my configuration, and that B037 has four explicit supporters and the broadest opening support (all eight ranked it, six in the top three). Two chemical-biology parts could also look uniform, and Somfai's point that code expansion is a tool for protein research more than a new way to make medicines is a fair description of its reach.

responses.point: Heiner's B037 case rests on one principle, induced proximity to an E3 ligase, and on a Crews, Deshaies and Handa trio that maps a design strand and a mechanistic strand onto three names.
responses.response: I take this more seriously after round 1 than I did in my opening. The case is coherent when the cereblon finding is read as showing that an old drug already acted by induced proximity, and the four supporters converge on the same trio, which does reduce my worry about arbitrary attribution. I still think the PROTAC concept and the cereblon mechanism are separate discoveries with different histories, and that omitting Ciulli, whose VHL ligands and ternary-complex work made degraders drug-like, is a real cost. I now accept that the missing PROTAC approval is a timing risk and not a scientific one, so B037 is my first fallback and I would not oppose it.

responses.point: Andrei moved from base editing to B037, argued that approval is not the test for a chemistry prize, and offered a two-part concept-plus-mechanism prize if Sakamoto cannot be omitted. He also treats base editing as a strong later candidate because of the 2020 CRISPR prize and safety data.
responses.response: I agree with you that drug approval is not the test: the proximity mechanism is settled, and that moved me toward B037. On B060 I do not think the 2020 prize makes base editing premature. CRISPR nucleases cut DNA, whereas a deaminase fusion changes one base chemically, so a Liu citation describes a different chemical step, and I would frame it that way. I accept your point on safety and on Nishida and Kondo, and that is why I pair B060 with the more mature B002 and do not offer it alone. Your concept-plus-mechanism split is the honest answer to the Sakamoto problem, but it would need two parts and so does not fit with my own pairing within three names.

responses.point: Peter prefers Deshaies over Ciulli in the third B037 slot because Crews and Deshaies made the founding heterobifunctional degrader, and says B002 credit is as entangled as B037 and its impact is as a protein-research tool.
responses.response: The founding-act argument for Deshaies over Ciulli is reasonable and I no longer press Ciulli as hard, although I would still call it a judgement. On B002 I partly accept your criticism: Wang's early experimental work is a real credit question, and I cannot claim the B002 boundary is cleaner than B037. I would still defend Schultz and Chin, because Schultz built the first general orthogonal pairs and Chin generalised the approach to multiple and quadruplet codons and to other organisms. I do not agree that a tool-like reach is a weakness, since the genetic-code work enabled many experimental fields and it is chemistry by construction.

responses.point: Peter prefers B005 (Buchwald and Hartwig) as mature, clean and overdue, and considers B037 and clinical validation still maturing.
responses.response: I agree that B005 is mature and well attributed, and Somfai and Zou make the Kosugi precursor point less decisive than it first looks, since the generality came from the ligand work. My difference remains novelty relative to the 2010 prize: C-N coupling extends a catalytic logic already honoured, whereas genetic code expansion and base editing add new capabilities. That keeps B005 as my second fallback. If attribution clarity becomes the committee's deciding criterion, it is the better prize than my own configuration, and I would vote for it before voting for a B037 trio that I think leaves out Ciulli.

responses.point: Emma moved from Ciulli to Handa and now sees cereblon as a decisive mechanistic discovery that stands on its own, but she notes that B037 may be read as drug modality rather than chemistry.
responses.response: Your move to Handa is the strongest argument I have seen for the trio, since the cereblon result is what gave the glue strand a mechanism. I share your worry that B037 could be read as drug modality, and it is the reason I weigh chemical invention above clinical reach. On balance I read it as chemistry, because the idea rests on designed molecular recognition and ternary-complex thermodynamics, which is your own field. I would be comfortable if the committee settles on it.

uncertainties: Whether the committee judges B002 and B060 as a pair or prefers a single part, and whether Lei Wang's early experimental role outweighs Chin's later extensions.
Whether base editing is read as distinct from the 2020 CRISPR prize, and how much the Nishida and Kondo report and the accumulating clinical safety data should weigh against a Liu-alone citation.
Whether B037 reaches five votes with a trio that omits Ciulli and Sakamoto, and whether a first regulatory approval of a degrader before the decision would settle its maturity case.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict with any shortlisted candidate. My postdoc mentors (Molly Stevens, Freddy Boey) and my Linköping colleagues are not credited on any shortlisted ballot. My research on peptide self-assembly and condensed phases overlaps with B024, which I do not propose, and genetic code expansion is a tool of interest to my own peptide and biomaterials work, but I have no personal or institutional tie to Schultz, Chin or Liu. No recusal is needed.
